title: Sanitizer run
description: A machine-checkable record of one dynamic sanitizer run (V2-35): AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, ThreadSanitizer, MemorySanitizer or LeakSanitizer. A sanitizer finding is runtime evidence that a claim about memory or undefined behaviour is false, so the record carries how the run ended and the bytes it printed. L2 hashes the output, ties finished_at to the evidence date, and rejects a record that declares a clean run while the output carries a sanitizer finding line. The record does not prove that the build was instrumented, that the corpus exercised the claim, or that the sanitizer would have caught a different defect; an `anchor` is required (an SSH signature over the record's canonical bytes, tools/anchor_subject.py) and L2 verifies it against the committed allowed_signers, but the key holder can re-sign and a replaced allowed_signers bypasses it (C-13).

tool.description: Sanitizer that instrumented the build. Lsan is listed separately because a leak-only run is not an address run.

version.description: Toolchain version, e.g. 'rustc 1.101.0-nightly'. A sanitizer's answer can change with the compiler and runtime version.

build_flags.description: Flags that instrumented the build, e.g. '-Zsanitizer=address'. A run without recorded instrumentation flags cannot be told apart from an ordinary test run.

command.description: Exact command that ran the instrumented tests, including the environment that set the flags.

exit_code.description: Process exit code. A non-zero code cannot support a non-open status.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Its local date must equal the evidence date.

output.description: Path to the captured sanitizer output, relative to --tool-output-root (default: the project root at --root), or a URL, in which case the hash is not checked.

output_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the output bytes. Lint check L2 verifies it.

status.description: How the run ended (V2-28 vocabulary). completed — the process exited before any bound; exit_code is the sanitizer's own. unverified — the run was cut short or the supervisor could not decide; it cannot support a non-open claim. failed — non-zero exit before the bound. error — the wrapper could not start or supervise the process.

anchor.description: An SSH signature over the canonical bytes of the sanitizer run (tool, version, build flags, command, exit code, timestamps, output hash, status; see tools/anchor_subject.py). The signed subject, its signature and the allowed_signers file are committed and hashed here. L2 recomputes the bytes and verifies the signature, so a record edited after signing stops verifying. The private key is not in the repository. The anchor does not stop the key holder, or anyone who can replace allowed_signers and re-sign: that is the remaining C-13 gap.

type.description: Signature scheme. Only ssh-ed25519 is implemented.

signer.description: Identity passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify -I`; must appear in allowed_signers.

namespace.description: Signature namespace (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -n`). Pinned per channel: a static-analysis or run-record signature does not verify here.

subject.description: Path to the signed canonical subject, relative to --tool-output-root.

subject_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the subject bytes. L2 verifies it.

signature.description: Path to the detached SSH signature (`ssh-keygen -Y sign` output).

signature_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signature file. L2 verifies it.

allowed_signers.description: Path to the committed allowed_signers file used for verification.

date.description: Date the signature was made. For a backfilled record this is later than the run's finished_at: the signature proves immutability after signing, not the run date.
